docs.title: MedOmni
docs.text:
The open-source ecosystem for omni-modality medical intelligence. MedOmni is open infrastructure for medical AI on any data modality: tables, waveforms, images, volumes and notes.

A clinician reads lab tables, ECGs, sleep recordings, X-rays, retinal scans and notes side by side. MedOmni aims to be the shared, open infrastructure where agents and models learn to do the same: take in any medical data modality, be tested on it, and improve. A dataset or encoder added to MedOmni once can be used by every agent and model tested on it.

MedOmni is a shared Core with projects built on it. Each project depends on Core, and the projects exchange data only through Core's contracts, so each can be used and changed on its own.

This is v0.3.0, the first public release

MedOmni v0.3.0 (git tag v0.3.0) is the first public release and the first milestone of MedOmni. It has:

  • the medomni package and command
  • versioned contracts shared by all projects
  • extension points for agents, datasets, tasks and encoders, filled by pull request or plug-in package without changing Core

docs.title: Data use and patient privacy
docs.text: MedOmni works in a sensitive medical domain, and we respect the data use agreement of every dataset it supports. No patient data ships with MedOmni: you build tasks from generated dummy data, open datasets such as VitalDB, or your own licensed copy of a dataset such as MIMIC-IV, and what is built from patient data stays on your machine.

docs.title: What v0.3.0 includes
docs.text:
The projects and the core they share:

Project Does Package Command Bench Runs AI agents on built medical tasks and scores them, whoever built the tasks. A task gives an agent one patient's evidence and a clinical question; a fixed verifier scores the answer. It scores the agent as a whole (scaffold and model), as Terminal-Bench and SWE-bench do. medomni.bench medomni bench Perception Serves medical encoders through an HTTP gateway. Each encoder reads one kind of input, such as a 12-lead ECG, and returns evidence for an agent or your own code. medomni.perception medomni perception Studio Makes and builds tasks: dataset survey, task proposals from clinicians, review and sign-off, cohort previews, MedOmni's task builder, the audit and reports. medomni.studio medomni studio Core Shared by every project: the contracts, the medomni command, plug-in loading, dataset loading, the family converter interface, the cache, the built-task contract and the testing kit. medomni.core medomni

Not in v0.3.0: MedOmni Agent (a later project) and a PyPI release.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text: Bench and Perception each have their own package and content folder, and depend only on Core. Studio sits above both: its builder writes built tasks, which Bench runs and scores. Inside a task, the agent calls Perception's encoders through the perception service: Perception's gateway, which Bench starts beside the agent, with a call budget and a call log. Tasks, traces and results stay on your machine. Architecture shows the layout.

docs.title: Get started
docs.text: From install to a scored Bench run: first on dummy data, which needs no credentials, then on real data. To use only the encoders, see Use the encoders.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Python 3.11 or later, Docker and uv.
  • A model for your agent: a local model server, or an API key for a model provider.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
git clone --branch v0.3.0 https://github.com/medomni/MedOmni medomni && cd medomni

uv venv && source .venv/bin/activate && uv pip install -e .

medomni --version

MedOmni writes your configuration, built tasks, runs and results to the workspace: ~/.medomni, or the folder in MEDOMNI_HOME. Nothing in it is committed or uploaded.

docs.title: 2. Describe your agent
docs.text:
Copy the agent template and set your model. See Test your agent for every field.

medomni bench agent new my-agent

docs.title: 3. Run on dummy data
docs.text:
Dummy data is generated from the dataset packages and each family's declared format. It needs no credentials and contains no patient values. To look at it, medomni studio dummy <dataset> --out <dir> writes one dataset's dummy data to a folder.

medomni studio task build --set medomni-bench/smoke-dummy

Studio's builder, medomni-v1, writes the set's built tasks to your workspace. Bench runs and scores them.

The set's arm gives the agent encoders, which run as images on your machine. Before the first run, build them:

  • Each encoder you want the agent to have: medomni perception check perception/encoders/<family>/<encoder> --record builds its image, checks it on its test data and records it. The perception service serves only recorded images.

  • Then the perception service, which carries the record:

    docker build -f src/medomni/perception/sidecar/Dockerfile -t medomni-perception .

    medomni bench run refuses to start without it and prints this command.

For a provider's API, export its key in the same shell first, such as export OPENAI_API_KEY=....

medomni bench run --agent my-agent.yaml --set medomni-bench/smoke-dummy

medomni bench run runs every atom task in Harbor and records each run in its run folder.

docs.title: 4. Score
docs.text:
medomni bench score --set medomni-bench/smoke-dummy

It prints one row per task, target, agent and arm: the score, the number of patients and the failure rate. Scores on dummy data only show that the pipeline works.

docs.title: 5. Run on real data
docs.text:
MedOmni hosts no dataset. Download and connect each dataset as in Connect your data, then build its task set as in Rebuild a task set:

  • VitalDB is open and needs no access request: medomni-bench/vitaldb.
  • MIMIC-IV, AI-READI and BDSP need your own access: medomni-bench/v1.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
The medomni package has one subpackage per project. The command calls these modules; use them directly to script MedOmni from Python.

Module Holds medomni.core.contracts The versioned contracts: a typed model and a validator for each. See Contracts. medomni.core.plugins Finds the projects' entry points, and the plug-in packages' content folders and entry points. medomni.core.testing The check runner, for use in a plug-in package's own tests. medomni.core.cli The medomni command. medomni.core.loading The format readers, and the loader that runs a dataset package through them into its event table. medomni.core.families The family registry, the converter interface and the dummy-data generator (medomni.core.families.dummy). medomni.core.tasks Built tasks: the atom layout, task sets, the checks on built tasks and the atom's shared Harbor parts. See Built tasks. medomni.core.builders TaskBuilder, the interface every task builder follows, and the medomni.builders group. medomni.core.cache The cache backend call, the folder and none backends, and the cache commands. medomni.bench.runs The runner interface, the agent runner on Harbor, and the replay agent (which repeats recorded runs with no model calls); run and prediction records. medomni.bench.arms The run side of the four built-in arms. medomni.bench.scoring The scorer and the behaviour metrics. medomni.bench.metrics The metrics auc, qwk and mae. medomni.perception.registry The encoder catalogue: model cards, image builds and pulls. medomni.perception.runtime The encoder interface, one decoder per family, and the serving code built into every image. medomni.perception.gateway The gateway service: catalogue, router and evidence. medomni.perception.sidecar The perception service: the gateway beside each atom task's agent, with the call budget, family filter and call log. Bench starts it through medomni.services. medomni.studio.build The medomni-v1 builder: its recipe format (medomni.studio.build.contracts) and engine, the task steps, cohort selection, its checks, the arms' build side and config hashes. medomni.studio The tools around Bench and Perception, one subpackage per kind: survey, propose, review (with the audit), preview, assets, report.
  • medomni.core imports no project.
  • medomni.bench and medomni.perception import only medomni.core, never each other.
  • medomni.studio may import medomni.core, medomni.bench and medomni.perception. Nothing imports it.
  • Projects register their commands, checks and audit checks with Core; see How Core finds the projects.

docs.title: Commands
docs.text: Shared commands are at the top level; each project's commands are under its name. Every subcommand prints its options with --help, and every check exits 1 on any failure.

docs.title: Core
docs.text: Command Does medomni --version Prints the MedOmni version. medomni plugins Lists the installed plug-in packages and what each adds, arms included. medomni contracts check [<contract> ...] Validates every contract file in the repository and in the installed plug-in packages: family registry, dataset config, dataset policy, recipe, task template, agent config, benchmark card, task set, model card. Name families, datasets, policies, recipes, templates, agents, benchmarks, sets or cards to check only those. medomni cache build <dataset> Loads the dataset's event table into the cache. medomni cache status Lists the cached results per dataset and step, with size and use. folder backend only. medomni cache gc [--dry-run] Removes results no current step uses, and unfinished folders. folder backend only.

docs.title: Bench
docs.text: Command Does medomni bench data connect <dataset> --path <dir> Records where your copy of a dataset is, in the workspace configuration. medomni bench agent new <name> Writes an agent config to fill in. medomni bench run --agent <config> --set <set> Runs the checks on built tasks, the stand-in agents and the route check on the built set, and runs nothing if one fails. Then runs every atom task in Harbor and records each run. Prints a running count of finished and failed atom tasks. --arm (repeatable; default: every arm the set lists). Resumes where it stopped. medomni bench score --set <set> Scores every target of every complete <template>@<cohort> per agent, arm and repetition, and prints and saves the table. Rows with different config hashes are flagged configured differently. The only command that writes scores. --agent limits it to one agent.

docs.title: Perception
docs.text: Command Does medomni perception pull [<family-or-encoder> ...] Pulls encoder images from ghcr.io/medomni. Nothing is published there yet; build images with perception check. medomni perception up --data-root <dir> Starts the gateway on the pulled encoders, on 127.0.0.1:8000. medomni perception new <family>/<encoder> Writes an encoder folder to fill in, in perception/encoders/, with an empty testdata/. medomni perception check <encoder-folder> Validates the model card with contracts check, checks the Dockerfile's torch installs, builds the image, checks the torch inside it is a listed CPU build, and runs the encoder's tests: compares its responses on test data with expected.json, then on real family samples from --samples <dir>, or reports that stage unverified without them; --freeze records expected.json instead; --record writes a passing encoder into perception/deployed.yaml, the images the perception service starts.

docs.title: Studio
docs.text: Command Does medomni studio data new <dataset> Writes a dataset package to fill in, in studio/datasets/<dataset>/. medomni studio data check <dataset> Checks the package's files and policy, writes and loads its dummy data, and checks your copy: version, listed files, the columns the readers need, each hook's problems, and that every raw value a label reads is classified (dataset check). It never loads your copy; medomni cache build does. medomni studio task new <template> --dataset <dataset> Writes a task template and an n20 cohort to fill in. medomni studio task build --set <set> or <template>@<cohort> Runs Build, the medomni-v1 builder: built tasks in the workspace, for every arm the set lists. --set rebuilds a published set from your copy, with the builder the set names. A pair alone is built under encoders, or under the arms --arm names. Dummy data for medomni-bench/smoke-dummy is generated on the fly. medomni studio task check <template>@<cohort> Checks a template, its cohort and the build: fields, metrics, labels, test patients, families, the builder's correctness checks, and Core's checks on built tasks. medomni studio task check --set <set> Runs the checks of task check <template>@<cohort> on every pair the set pins. medomni studio task check --release For MedOmni's releases: checks every pinned pair in every task set, and fails when a pair's cohort, labels, targets, scoring or dataset release changed since the last release and its version N has not risen. It compares config files, never data. Builds and runs never use it. medomni studio survey <dataset> Reports what a dataset has: codes, families, time spans and counts, from its event table. medomni studio census <set> For each built pair and arm of a set: the families staged and the spread of the answers. medomni studio intake <file> Turns the rows of an intake form into draft proposals, or a signed-off proposal into a task template. medomni studio review-form <template>@<cohort> Writes the task's clinical review form. --submit <file> records a filled-in form as the task's review. medomni studio preview <template>@<cohort> Runs the cohort on your copy up to cohort selection and prints the patients left after each step and per class. Builds nothing. medomni studio download-list <dataset> Lists what to download for a dataset: one tab-separated line per entry, with its source, its path in your copy and how to fetch it (file, folder or gunzip). Without the index tables on disk, it prints those first. medomni studio dummy <dataset> [--subjects N] [--seed S] [--out DIR] Writes dummy data shaped like the dataset, from its dataset.yaml and codes.csv, with the dummy-data generator. medomni studio release-check Checks that the release tree may be published: encoder card licences against image licence labels (--no-images skips Docker), dataset publish rules, a licensed PROVENANCE beside every data file, and task set versions. See Release check. medomni studio audit Runs the audit and writes its report to the workspace. --only limits it to some assets. medomni studio progress <run> Shows a run's progress live, per atom task. Run it beside medomni bench run. medomni studio build-sheet <set> Writes a sheet of what a set's build made, per task, to the workspace. medomni studio bench-health <run> Reports each encoder's health from a finished run's call log. medomni studio tables Writes the results table of the scored runs. --set <set> limits it to one task set. medomni studio diagrams <description> Draws the architecture diagrams from one YAML description, as SVG files that also open in draw.io. medomni studio relevance <template> Writes the relevance table that scoring reads for a template. medomni studio encoder-status Lists which encoders are built and which are planned. medomni studio encoder-demo <encoder> Runs an encoder on one sample and prints its evidence. medomni studio testdata <encoder> Writes an encoder's test inputs and PROVENANCE.md into its testdata/. medomni studio family-samples <family> Writes samples of a family from your copy of a dataset, for real-sample checks. They hold patient data and stay in your workspace. medomni studio check <tool> Checks a tool against its kind's interface.

docs.title: Add a dataset
docs.text: For a new openly licensed dataset, such as VitalDB, read by MedOmni's builder, medomni-v1. Pull requests add datasets only when openly licensed; use a plug-in package for others.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The dataset's license allows redistribution of samples (for example CC BY 4.0).
  • Its recordings map to existing families. See Families.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the dataset package:

    medomni studio data new my-dataset

  2. Write dataset.yaml: the description (unit, kind of time, version), the format readers and what each reads, the dataset's rules, and any family converters its raw files need. See Datasets reference.

  3. List every code the dataset emits in codes.csv. Use the shared codes where the dataset has those concepts.
  4. Write labels.yaml and evidence.yaml. See Recipes reference.
  5. Write the dataset policy from the license: what may be published and which routes may see the data.

  6. Generate dummy data from your package and check that it has the tables and codes you expect. It comes from dataset.yaml and codes.csv, with no extra file.

    medomni studio dummy my-dataset --subjects 20 --out ~/dummy/my-dataset

  7. Optional: add the package's dummy data, from medomni studio dummy, to MedOmni's public Hugging Face repository. It holds dummy data only, never real records. Nothing in Build reads it.

  8. Add at least one template and cohort, as in Add a task, and open a pull request.

Python goes only in hooks/: for a label no rule can express, and download.py, which tells medomni studio download-list where the dataset's files come from. See Hooks. A file format no format reader knows needs a new format reader in Core: open an issue first.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni studio data check my-dataset

It checks the package's files and policy, writes and loads its dummy data, and checks that every code is in codes.csv.

Submit it as a pull request, or ship it in your own plug-in package. Contribute covers both.

docs.title: Add a task
docs.text: For a task on a supported dataset, using labels and families MedOmni already has, or labels you add to the dataset's library.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the template and a first cohort:

    medomni studio task new vitaldb_my-task --dataset vitaldb

  2. Fill in template.yaml: the targets with each one's label and metric, the input, and the agent block with the statement, the prediction-time paragraph, environment and submission path. Give each label a question, or give the target its own. The agent sees the patient's whole record minus the labels' guards, so do not list leaking evidence again. The fields are in Tasks reference.

  3. Write a cohort in cohorts/: source population, prediction time, requirements and cohort selection (select). Add its test patients. See Recipes reference.

  4. Preview the counts on your copy, adjust the cohort, then build.

    medomni studio preview vitaldb_my-task@n20
medomni studio task build vitaldb_my-task@n20

  5. Open a pull request with the template folder.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni studio task check vitaldb_my-task@n20

It checks:

  • the template's fields and metrics
  • that each target's label is in the library and states its window
  • that the cohort's test patients give their expected results
  • the correctness checks: no answer in the evidence, events still ahead and images before the prediction time, enough patients, answers that vary, complete recordings, a closed network
  • that staged files match their families

Submit it as a pull request, or ship it in your own plug-in package. Contribute covers both.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:

  • Tasks reference: the task template contract.
  • Recipes reference: the cohort, label and evidence fields.

docs.title: Add an encoder
docs.text: For a new encoder that reads an existing family. Encoder folders live in perception/encoders/ and are built into images; they are not part of the installed package.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• The encoder reads one existing family. Its code, weights and test data have licenses that allow you to package them.
  • Test data for the family: synthetic or openly licensed, with a provenance note.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the encoder folder:

    medomni perception new <family>/<encoder>

    It writes:

    perception/encoders/<family>/<encoder>/
├── adapter.py
├── card.yaml
├── Dockerfile
├── assets.json
└── testdata/       empty, filled in step 4

  2. Implement the adapter and pin the image:

    • encode(sample, options) in adapter.py, with expensive set-up in load()
    • base image, dependencies and source revision pinned in the Dockerfile
    • torch, if the encoder needs it, installed with torch==<version> from the CPU build index, at a version listed in src/medomni/perception/registry/torch.yaml
    • weights and other files in assets.json, each with its source (a URL or a Hugging Face file) and sha256; the image build fetches and checks them
  3. Write the model card: the family, outputs, options, license and source. See Encoders.

  4. Write the test data, its inputs and PROVENANCE.md:

    medomni studio testdata <family>__<encoder>

  5. Record the expected responses on the test data, and open a pull request.

    medomni perception check perception/encoders/<family>/<encoder> --freeze

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni perception check perception/encoders/<family>/<encoder>

It validates the model card with medomni contracts check, checks the Dockerfile's torch installs against the list, builds the image, checks the torch inside it is a listed CPU build, and runs the encoder's tests: it runs the image on the test data and compares the responses with expected.json. See Check and freeze. GPU encoders may run on a self-hosted runner.

Submit it as a pull request, or ship it in your own plug-in package. Contribute covers both.

docs.title: Connect your data
docs.text: For agent evaluators who build tasks on a real dataset. Every dataset is set up the same way, open or credentialed: get access, download your copy, tell MedOmni where it is, check it and build its cache. MedOmni hosts no dataset: you download each one from its owner.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Access granted by the data owner, under its license: PhysioNet credentialing for MIMIC-IV, the AI-READI data license, the BDSP data use agreement. VitalDB is open and needs none. MedOmni cannot grant or check access for you.
  • Read the dataset's row in Datasets for what its license permits.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. List what to download, then download it:

    medomni studio download-list mimic-iv

    It writes one tab-separated line per entry: the source, the path in your copy, and how to fetch it: file, folder (copied whole) or gunzip (decompressed on the way). The list is chosen from the dataset's index tables, so fetch those first: without them, it prints the index entries to download and stops.

    Dataset Source What is listed MIMIC-IV PhysioNet Core 3.1 and ED 2.2 whole; CXR-JPG 2.1.0, MIMIC-IV-ECG 1.0 and the Waveform Database 0.1.0 for the source population only. Their indexes are the CXR metadata and image list, the ECG record_list.csv and the waveform RECORDS. AI-READI FAIRhub Each participant's files, by the package's folder patterns. BDSP BDSP's S3 access point The index tables, then each source-population patient's latest night. About 349 listed scoring files are not on the server, because those nights were never scored, so a missing scoring file is expected. VitalDB VitalDB's open API, api.vitaldb.net The clinical, lab and track tables, then each case's .vital file. The package uses the API's file names, which differ from those of VitalDB's copy on PhysioNet.

  2. Tell MedOmni where your copy is. The path is recorded in your workspace config.

    medomni bench data connect mimic-iv --path /path/to/mimic-iv

  3. Check your copy against the dataset package, without loading it: the version, the files the package lists, the columns the readers need, and that every raw value a label reads is classified.

    medomni studio data check mimic-iv

  4. Load the dataset's event table into the cache.

    medomni cache build mimic-iv

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni studio data check names each problem it finds and exits 1:

  • a version that differs from the one the package describes
  • a file the package lists that is missing
  • a table or column the format readers need that is missing
  • a raw value a label reads that the label library does not classify

Fix your copy and run it again. When it passes, build a task set as in Rebuild a task set.

Keep data local

The cache, built atom tasks, answers, traces and the results file contain patient data. Do not commit, upload or share them.

docs.title: Contribute
docs.text: For contributors who add an agent to Bench, a dataset or a task to Studio, or an encoder to Perception.

docs.title: How MedOmni is developed
docs.text:
MedOmni is developed in a private repository. The public repository is an export of each release, and every commit in it keeps its author.

A pull request goes to the public repository:

  1. Create the starting files with the piece's new command, fill them in, and run its check command locally.
  2. Open a pull request on the public repository. CI runs the same check, and the MedOmni team reviews it.
  3. Once it is merged there, it is brought into development under your name and ships in the next release.

Work that should stay in your own repository, for example a task on data that cannot leave your institution, can be a plug-in package instead: your own medomni-* package that ships the same pieces in a content folder and runs the same check. See Publish a plug-in package.

Contributions change only extension points. Only the MedOmni team changes Core and the contracts; if you need a contract change, such as a new family, open an issue first.

Every model card and task template lists its authors.

docs.title: What you can add
docs.text:
• Add an encoder: a new encoder for an existing family.
  • Add a dataset: a new openly licensed dataset, read by MedOmni's builder.
  • Add a task: a template and a cohort on a supported dataset.
  • An agent, below.

docs.title: Add an agent (Bench)
docs.text: For a new scaffold or model.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create the agent config and fill it in, as in Test your agent.

    medomni bench agent new my-agent

  2. Open a pull request adding it as bench/agents/<name>.yaml.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni bench run --agent my-agent.yaml --set medomni-bench/smoke-dummy

Every atom task of medomni-bench/smoke-dummy must finish with a run and no infrastructure error.

docs.title: Publish a plug-in package
docs.text: For agents, datasets, tasks or encoders that live in your own repository.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Create a Python package named medomni-<name> that depends on medomni.
  2. Add a content folder to the package, laid out like MedOmni's repository: bench/agents/, studio/datasets/<dataset>/, bench/benchmarks/<benchmark>/, perception/encoders/<family>/<encoder>/. Create each piece in it as on the Add pages.

  3. Register the folder with one entry point in pyproject.toml:

    [project.entry-points."medomni.plugins"]
myname = "medomni_myname:content"

    A family converter, a task builder, an arm or a Studio tool is Python code: register it in medomni.converters, medomni.builders, medomni.arms (with its build side in medomni.arm_builds) or medomni.tools. A converter for one dataset's own format is declared in its dataset.yaml instead. See Plug-ins.

  4. In your package's tests, run the same checks with medomni.core.testing.

  5. Install it as a wheel or in editable mode. Zip installs are not supported.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni plugins

Your package and each piece it adds are listed, and the check commands (medomni studio task check, medomni perception check and the rest) work on them as on built-in pieces.

docs.title: Rebuild a task set
docs.text: For agent evaluators who want to run on a published task set, such as medomni-bench/v1, built from their own copy of the data. You build every <template>@<cohort> in the set from its config with Studio's builder, medomni-v1, and check each build. Bench then runs the built set.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Your copy of each dataset in the set is connected. See Connect your data.
  • Space for the cache and the atom tasks in your workspace, on a disk with room for the dataset copies you use.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Build the cache for each dataset in the set.

    medomni cache build mimic-iv

  2. Build the set. Every <template>@<cohort> in it is built under every arm the set lists, by the builder the set names.

    medomni studio task build --set medomni-bench/v1

  3. Check every build.

    medomni studio task check --set medomni-bench/v1

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni studio task check --set medomni-bench/v1 runs the checks of medomni studio task check <template>@<cohort> on every pair in the set, and lists each pair as passing or failing. medomni bench run runs the checks on built tasks again before it starts.

Your results carry each task's config hash. Results with the same config hash used the same task config; the hash doesn't show that your copy of the data matches. To compare a build with someone else's, compare the per-step patient counts in your build manifests by hand.

Keep data local

The cache, built atom tasks, answers, traces and the results file contain patient data. Do not commit, upload or share them.

docs.title: Where next
docs.text:
• Test your agent: run on the set you built.
  • Build: the steps the counts come from.
  • Cache: what the cache holds.

docs.title: Test your agent
docs.text: For agent evaluators. You evaluate how your agent performs on MedOmni's medical tasks under the conditions you choose, such as with and without encoders, and read the scores.

docs.title: What you can test
docs.text:
A task set fixes the tasks; an arm fixes the conditions the agent works under. A set lists the arms it is built for, and every score row names its arm, so you compare one agent across arms, or several agents under one arm.

Arm The agent gets encoders The patient's evidence and the encoders for the families it holds. no-perception The same evidence, with no encoders. encoders-required The evidence and the encoders, and it must call at least one. modality-ladder Six rungs, each adding input families to the last, to show how performance changes as modalities are added. Task set Holds Arms medomni-bench/smoke-dummy One pair per template, on generated data: checks that the pipeline works. encoders medomni-bench/v1 The credentialed templates. encoders, no-perception medomni-bench/vitaldb The VitalDB templates, on an open dataset. encoders, no-perception medomni-bench/modality-ladder The ladder templates at their ladder cohort. modality-ladder

Runs explains arms, and Tasks the task sets.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
• Get started working end to end on medomni-bench/smoke-dummy.
  • The task set built from your data. See Rebuild a task set.

docs.title: Steps
docs.text:
1. Describe your agent in an agent config, starting from the template:

    medomni bench agent new my-agent

    kind: agent
name: my-agent
model: openai/my-model
route: cloud
settings:
  scaffold: terminus-2
  model_served: my-model-2026-10-01
  env:
    OPENAI_API_KEY: ${OPENAI_API_KEY}
  max_turns: 300
    Field Meaning kind The kind of intelligence: agent. name The agent's name, as records show it. model The model to request. route local for a model served on your machine, cloud for a provider's API. Bench refuses a run on a route a dataset's policy denies, and prints the conditions of a conditional route, which you must meet; see Datasets. runner Optional: a runner other than the kind's own. MedOmni's tests use runner: replay. settings What the runner reads. For the agent runner, on Harbor, the fields below; the runner checks them. settings.scaffold The Harbor agent that drives the model. settings.model_served The model name the provider reports back. A requested alias can be served by a different model; a run that reports another name is recorded as an error and never scored. settings.env Keys, only as ${VARNAME} references to variables you export in the shell that runs medomni bench run. Never write a key into the config: on a cloud route the runner refuses a key that is not a reference. settings.max_turns The most turns the agent may take on one atom task. settings.api_base The provider's base URL, for a model server on your machine or a compatible API.

  2. Export your model provider's key in your shell, then run the agent on a task set, under each arm you want to compare:

    export OPENAI_API_KEY=...

    medomni bench run --agent my-agent.yaml --set medomni-bench/v1 --arm encoders --arm no-perception

    Without --arm, it runs every arm the set lists. medomni bench run first checks the built tasks, and resumes if run again. Runs explains both. While it runs, it prints one line with the number of finished and failed atom tasks; for a detailed live view, run medomni studio progress <run> beside it.

  3. Score:

    medomni bench score --set medomni-bench/v1 --agent my-agent

docs.title: Check
docs.text: medomni bench score prints the task × target × agent × arm table and writes it to the workspace. Each row has the score, patient count, failure rate, cost and encoder use. Scoring lists when a score is refused.

docs.title: Results file
docs.text:
Every run and every score is one result record. Run records are lines of runs.jsonl in each run folder; score records are lines of results.jsonl in your workspace. You need them only to analyse results beyond the table. Scoring explains how it is written.

Contract: result record, src/medomni/core/contracts/schemas/result-record.schema.json.

Record One per Key fields Run (kind: run) agent run on one atom task run_id, task_set (<benchmark>/<set>), task (<template>@<cohort>), task_version (N.X), intelligence (kind: agent and its name), config_hash, model_served, error_kind, api_cost; in its agent block: arm, arm_variant (the ladder's rung, r1 to r6), encoders_served, encoder_calls, files_opened Score (kind: score) task × target × agent × arm × repetition run_id, task_set, task_set_hash, target, config_hash, task_version, intelligence, arm and arm_variant when the runs had them, n_atoms, n_failed, metric, value, flags, encoder_use

Result records are patient data

Run ids name the patients they ran on, so the run folders and the results file fall under each dataset's data use agreement. Keep them in the workspace.
