  • Built tasks: the files Build writes, and how to write your own builder.
  • Cache: what Build keeps between runs.
  • Tasks: templates, cohorts and task sets.

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
A dataset is a source of patient data used under its own license. MedOmni's builder, medomni-v1, reads it through its dataset package, and Bench obeys its dataset policy when it runs. MedOmni ships no data.

your copy ──loading: format readers + dataset package──▶ event table ──Build──▶ atom tasks
                         policy ──▶ which routes may see them

docs.title: Dataset package
docs.text:
One folder per dataset, studio/datasets/<dataset>/, read by the medomni-v1 builder. It is configuration, not code:

  • dataset.yaml: a description, the format readers to use, the dataset's rules and its named definitions, the dataset's own family converters, and the disk space each atom task gets (storage_mb)
  • labels.yaml: the label library
  • evidence.yaml: what an atom task may hold, relative to the prediction time
  • codes.csv: every code the dataset emits, with a description and its source table
  • policy.yaml: what the license allows
  • hooks/: Python for what only this dataset needs, such as CKD staging by KDIGO
  • converters/: the dataset's own family converters, such as BDSP's h5-to-edf
  • tasks/: the dataset's task templates and their cohorts

The description states the unit (a patient, a participant, a surgery case), the kind of time (date and time, visit dates only, seconds from case start) and the dataset version. Time is described, not converted: Build refuses a recipe the dataset's time cannot support.

docs.title: Loading
docs.text:
Loading turns your copy into the dataset's event table. It has two parts:

  • Format readers: shared code in Core, one per file format. A format reader knows a format and no dataset: it turns a CSV table, an OMOP table, a folder of files or a recording header into event rows.
  • The dataset package: configuration for one dataset. It names the format readers to use and what each reads: which files and columns, which column is the time, which code each row gets. Its visit rules say how events group into visits, such as one visit per participant.

The loader in Core runs the package through the format readers. v0.2 did both parts in one Python adapter per dataset. v0.3.0 has format readers for:

  • CSV tables
  • OMOP tables
  • folder trees, where a file's folder gives its family
  • recording headers: EDF, WFDB, HDF5 and DICOM

A dataset loads only the tables its recipes and labels use. A dataset in a format no format reader knows adds one to Core, which every later dataset can use.

docs.title: Event table
docs.text:
Every dataset becomes one event table, kept in the cache. It is the only thing later steps read.

Column Holds subject_id The unit: patient, participant or case time When the event happened; empty for static facts such as sex code What happened, such as ADMISSION or LAB//cr numeric_value, text_value The event's value, if any visit The visit the event belongs to
  • Column names follow MEDS, so MEDS tools can read the table.
  • Raw files are FILE//<family> rows, with a path relative to your copy, and optionally the file's own id (a DICOM UID, a WFDB record). Loading does not hash them; the cache keys each by a quick identity.
  • Annotations read from recordings, such as sleep stages, are events too.
  • A few codes are shared by every dataset; the rest are the dataset's own. See Shared codes.

Raw files are never copied into the table or the cache. Only files a family converter changes are written to the cache.

docs.title: Dataset policy
docs.text:
One policy per dataset, read from its license and data use agreement. It records:

  • what may be published: schema, templates, recipes, ID lists, labels, per-record outputs, samples
  • which model routes may see the data: local, cloud, or cloud under conditions
  • any limits on use, such as research only

Before a run, Bench checks the agent's route against the policy: a denied route refuses the run, and a conditional one prints the conditions you must meet. Nothing the policy denies is published. Recipes and config hashes contain no patient data, so every policy allows them.

docs.title: Open, credentialed and dummy data
docs.text:
Kind Examples What you need Credentialed MIMIC-IV, AI-READI, BDSP Your own access, then your own download. Open VitalDB Your own download; no access request. Dummy Generated Nothing. Made from the dataset package and each family's declared format, never from a real record.

MedOmni hosts no dataset, open or credentialed: you download every dataset yourself, with the list medomni studio download-list <dataset> writes, and the licenses differ only in each package's policy. MedOmni publishes recipes and config hashes, and, where a policy allows samples, a small data sample on Hugging Face. Build never reads a sample.

Dummy data lets every command run with no credentials. Its scores only show that the pipeline works.

  • A dataset's dummy data comes from its own dataset.yaml and codes.csv, with no extra file: the same tables, columns, codes and families, filled with generated values.
  • Every dataset package is loaded from its dummy data, so its configuration runs in CI.
  • medomni studio dummy <dataset> writes it to a folder, to look at or to run commands on.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
• studio/datasets/<dataset>/: the dataset package, with its own converters
  • src/medomni/core/loading/: the format readers and the loader
  • src/medomni/core/families/: the converter interface and the dummy-data generator
  • your workspace: the path to your copy, and the cache

docs.text:

  • Connect your data: connect and check your own copy.
  • Recipes: the queries that read the event table.

docs.title: Studio
docs.text:
Studio is the project that makes and builds tasks: surveying datasets, proposing and reviewing tasks, previewing cohorts, building them with MedOmni's task builder, auditing, and reporting results. Bench and Perception hold only what runs, scores and serves.

survey ──▶ propose ──▶ review and sign-off ──▶ frozen template + cohorts ──Build──▶ built tasks ──▶ Bench
                                                       preview on your copy ─┘
results ──▶ report, audit

docs.title: Build
docs.text:
Studio holds MedOmni's task builder, medomni-v1, with its inputs: the dataset packages, the task templates and cohorts and their recipes. Build runs them into built tasks, the files Bench reads.

medomni studio data new my-dataset                     # a dataset package to fill in
medomni studio data check mimic-iv                     # the package and your copy
medomni studio task new vitaldb_my-task --dataset vitaldb   # a template and an n20 cohort to fill in
medomni studio task build --set medomni-bench/v1       # build a published set, or name one <template>@<cohort>
medomni studio task check --set medomni-bench/v1       # the correctness checks on what was built

docs.title: The line between Studio and the other projects
docs.text:
With Studio removed, anyone can still run an agent on a built task set, score it and serve the encoders, with the same results. Anything that test does not need belongs in Studio.

  • Studio may import Core, Bench and Perception. Nothing imports Studio.
  • Studio writes to your workspace, or to its own content folder by pull request. Bench reads what Studio builds only through the built-task contract, so it runs a task from any builder the same way.
  • Patient-level outputs, such as survey counts per patient or review sheets with records, stay in your workspace. Proposals and forms hold no patient data.

docs.title: Tool kinds
docs.text:
Every Studio tool is one of six kinds. Each kind has one interface, so a new tool of that kind works with the same commands.

Kind Does In v0.3.0 survey Reports what a dataset has: codes, families, time spans, counts. Reads the event table. The dataset survey, the target census propose Makes content for a pull request: task proposals from clinicians, and the files people write by hand. Intake form and task catalogue, the relevance table scoring reads review Review forms and sign-off, status views, and the audit. Review forms, the audit, encoder status (which are built and which are planned) preview Shows what something does without building it. Cohort preview up to cohort selection, the files a source population needs, dummy data assets Works with the files encoders and families are checked on. An encoder demo on one sample, encoder test data, family samples report Tables, figures and views of builds and runs. Result tables, build sheets, a run's live progress, encoder health from a finished run, the architecture diagrams

docs.title: From proposal to built task
docs.text:
A task proposal moves through four states, recorded in its file:

  1. draft: written from the intake form
  2. under review: reviewers fill in the review form
  3. signed off: a named clinician and a MedOmni maintainer sign, with the date
  4. frozen: turned into a task template and cohorts, and opened as a pull request to studio/datasets/

A change to a frozen template is a new proposal, and raises the version of each of its cohorts.

docs.title: Add a tool
docs.text: A tool is a Python class of one kind, registered in the medomni.tools entry-point group, from MedOmni's repository or a plug-in package. medomni studio check <tool> checks that it follows its kind's interface and writes only to the workspace.

  • src/medomni/studio/: one subpackage per kind: survey/, propose/, review/ (with the audit), preview/, assets/, report/
  • studio/: content people write and review: datasets/ (the dataset packages, templates and cohorts)

  • Recipes: what preview runs.
  • Build: where a frozen template goes next.
  • Built tasks: what Build writes for Bench.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
A recipe says what Build, MedOmni's medomni-v1 builder, takes from a dataset. The recipe format is this builder's own; another builder can read other inputs. One format covers all of it:

  • cohort: who is included, and at which prediction time
  • labels: each target's answer
  • evidence: which rows, codes and files each patient's atom task holds

Each part is a set of queries over the dataset's event table. The queries name codes and windows; they never name patient ids. A cohort is therefore published as rules, never as a list of patients, which every dataset license allows.

docs.title: Where each part lives
docs.text:
Part File Written by Cohort cohorts/<cohort>.yaml, next to its template The task's authors Labels labels.yaml, in the dataset package The dataset's maintainers Evidence evidence.yaml, in the dataset package The dataset's maintainers

A template's targets name labels from the library, such as mimic-iv:ckd-kdigo. Templates on one dataset share its labels and its evidence rules.

docs.title: Cohort
docs.text:
A cohort file has five parts, run in this order:

  1. Source population: the patients a cohort may select from.
  2. Prediction time: an anchor event, such as an admission, plus an optional offset. Nothing after it is evidence.
  3. Requirements: events or files each patient must, or must not, have in a window, or a number of files that must convert.
  4. Labels: the targets' answers. A patient with no answer is left out.
  5. Cohort selection (the select field): how many patients per class, any labels that split each class further, and the seed.

docs.title: Source population
docs.text:
A patient is in the source population when sha256(salt|patient id), read as a fraction, is below f. The salt and the default f are in the dataset package.

  • The rule needs no list of ids, so it can be published.
  • Source populations nest: the patients at 1% are all in the 5% source population.
  • For a dataset whose files are downloaded only for the source population, such as BDSP's nights or MIMIC-IV's images and recordings, the rule runs on the dataset's index tables first, and Studio lists the files to download.

docs.title: Cohort selection
docs.text:
• n is split evenly across the classes of the by label. Any remainder goes to the first classes. With no by, as for a continuous target, the first n by rank are taken.
  • Within each class, patients are ranked by sha256(seed|patient id|prediction time) and the first k are taken.
  • balance names labels that split each class into groups, and n is split evenly across the groups as well. These labels are computed for cohort selection only, never scored or shown. A patient with no value for one is left out.
  • A class or group with too few patients stops the build. Other classes do not make up the shortfall.
  • A converts requirement is checked as cohort selection goes down the ranking: a patient whose files fail is replaced by the next one, so only the selected patients' files are converted.

Because cohort selection ranks by hash:

  • it is the same on every machine and Python version
  • the first 20 of a class at n = 50 are the patients selected at n = 20
  • one patient more or less in the pool changes at most one place

docs.title: Labels
docs.text:
Each entry in labels.yaml is one rule: a code, a window relative to the prediction time, and how the value is read (present, absent, last value, highest value, a threshold, bins). A label can count only events in the anchor's visit, or only events in other visits, such as for a readmission. A label that cannot be written as a rule calls a hook in the dataset package, such as CKD staging by KDIGO.

Each label also states its guard: the codes and fields that would reveal its answer. Build removes them from the evidence, matching rows by the event code they emit.

Each label has a question: the sentence that tells the agent exactly what the target asks. A template may give a target its own question instead.

Every label states its window. A label read from any time, before or after the prediction time, is allowed and is flagged by Build's check.

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text:
Per table, the evidence rules say:

  • which column holds the row's time; rows after the prediction time are left out
  • which fields are only known later, such as a discharge time, and are blanked while the stay is open
  • which rows belong to the patient's current visit and are left out or blanked
  • which rows are kept only when a linked row is kept, such as triage rows of a kept ED stay

Files are kept when their time is at or before the prediction time. A file with no time of its own that holds later rows, such as one table of a whole stay, is cut at the prediction time when its family is listed under files.crop.

The agent sees the whole record kept this way, minus the guard of every target. The template's input does not narrow it.

Two more parts of the evidence rules shape what the agent reads:

  • a views hook in the dataset package gives the forms the agent reads: the patient's demographics, one table of measurements, and details of each file
  • a reading_note tells the agent a fact about reading the dataset's files, in every arm

docs.title: Checks in every recipe
docs.text:
• Test patients. Each cohort comes with a few hand-written patients as event rows, and the expected result: in or out, prediction time, label values. They run in CI with no licensed data, so any copy of Build can be checked before it touches real data.
  • Step counts. Build records how many patients are left after each step. A rebuild that differs shows where.
  • Named definitions. A definition used by several recipes, such as "acute kidney injury", is defined once in the dataset package and named in each recipe.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
• src/medomni/studio/build/contracts/, recipes.py, labels.py, evidence.py: the recipe format, its validator and the engine that runs it
  • src/medomni/studio/schemas/: the format's JSON Schemas
  • studio/datasets/<dataset>/labels.yaml and evidence.yaml
  • studio/datasets/<dataset>/tasks/<template>/cohorts/: the cohorts and their test patients

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
A task asks a clinical question of each patient in a cohort, with a fixed way to score the answers. For MedOmni's builder, medomni-v1, it is written as a task template and one or more cohorts, and Build turns a template and a cohort into atom tasks. Bench runs the built task, whoever built it.

task template + cohort ──Build──▶ content of <template>@<cohort>, with the answers
                                        └──▶ one atom task per patient, per arm + config hash

docs.title: Task template
docs.text:
A YAML file, template.yaml, that states:

  • targets: one or more, each naming a label from the dataset's library and its metric, and optionally its own question
  • input: the tables and families the proposal named, kept as a record; the evidence is the patient's whole record minus the targets' guards
  • evidence: the evidence variants; v0.3.0 builds default only
  • agent: what an agent needs to run the task:
    • statement: the clinical question, which opens every atom task's instruction
    • instruction: the template's own paragraph on the prediction time
    • environment: CPUs, memory, timeouts, no internet
    • submission path: where the agent writes its answer

A template is frozen once its proposal is signed off in Studio. A later change to it raises the version of each of its cohorts.

docs.title: Cohort
docs.text:
A cohort is a recipe in its own file next to the template: who is included, at which prediction time, and how many per class. One template can have several cohorts, such as n20 and n50; the patients of n20 are the first ones of n50.

The pair is written <template>@<cohort>, such as mimic-iv_ckd-staging@n20. Each pair is one task.

docs.title: Version
docs.text:
Each task has a version N.X, kept as version: in its cohort file. Tasks start at 1.0.

  • N rises when results stop being comparable: a change to the dataset release, the cohort, the labels, the targets or the scoring.
  • X rises for any other change, such as the instruction's wording or how atom tasks are rendered.
  • A change to the template raises the version of each of its cohorts.
  • Task sets pin N. A change to X reaches every task set that holds the task; a new N enters only a new task set.

docs.title: Atom task
docs.text: The unit an agent runs: one patient, all of the targets, at the patient's prediction time. It holds the instruction, the patient's evidence, the environment and a format check. It never holds the answers. The agent writes one prediction per target. Its files are in Built tasks.

docs.title: Config hash
docs.text:
A hash of the config a task is built from under one arm: the template, the cohort, the labels and recipes it uses, the arm's definition, the builder's name and version, and the dataset and MedOmni releases. Runs with the same config hash used the same task configuration. Scores with different config hashes in one table are flagged; see Scoring.

The config hash covers no data; see Design principles.

docs.title: Task set
docs.text:
A named list of <template>@<cohort> pairs, each pinned at its version N, such as v1, and the arms to build them under. Task sets are what MedOmni publishes and what scores are compared on. A task set is a Core contract: Studio builds it, and Bench runs and scores it.

  • A task set only grows: pairs are added, never changed. A new N of a pair enters only a new task set, such as v2.
  • Its content hash covers every pair and its N. Each score record carries the hash, and scores with different hashes are never put in one table.
  • Credentialed task sets publish configs only; you build them from your own access. See Rebuild a task set.
  • The set names its builder, medomni-v1 for MedOmni's sets, which builds every pair under every arm the set lists.
  • To build outside a task set, for example while writing a cohort, name the pair: medomni studio task build mimic-iv_ckd-staging@n20.

docs.title: Benchmark
docs.text:
A benchmark holds several task sets under one card: its name, version, owner, license and the intelligence kinds it accepts. It is one folder, bench/benchmarks/<benchmark>/, with the card in benchmark.yaml and its task sets in sets/.

  • A task set is named <benchmark>/<set>, such as medomni-bench/v1, so two benchmarks can each have a v1.
  • MedOmni's own benchmark is medomni-bench. A plug-in package publishes its own benchmark as the same folder; see Plug-ins.

docs.title: Where it lives
docs.text:
• studio/datasets/<dataset>/tasks/<template>/: template.yaml and cohorts/
  • bench/benchmarks/<benchmark>/: a benchmark's card and its task sets
  • src/medomni/studio/build/: Build
  • your workspace: the built atom tasks and the cache

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text:
Every dataset v0.3.0 builds tasks from, with how to get access and what its policy allows, and the fields of a dataset package.

Contracts: dataset config, dataset-config.schema.json, and dataset policy, dataset-policy.schema.json, in src/medomni/core/contracts/schemas/. Each dataset has one package, in studio/datasets/<dataset>/, which MedOmni's builder, medomni-v1, reads with its own stricter v1-dataset-config.schema.json, in src/medomni/studio/schemas/.

Not legal advice

Each policy summarises the data owner's license and data use agreement. You are responsible for following your agreement. Before a run, Bench checks the agent's route against the policy of each dataset in the task set, but it cannot check a route's conditions for you.

docs.title: Source populations
docs.text:
Each cohort selects from its dataset's source population: the patients for whom sha256(salt|patient id), read as a fraction, is below the default fraction. A cohort may set a smaller fraction.

Dataset Unit Default source population MIMIC-IV Patient 5% of patients AI-READI Participant All BDSP Patient at site I0006 10% of patients; download only their latest sleep study, listed by medomni studio download-list bdsp VitalDB Surgery case All

docs.title: Dataset package
docs.text:
File Required Holds dataset.yaml yes The dataset config, below. labels.yaml yes The label library. See Recipes. evidence.yaml yes The evidence rules. See Recipes. codes.csv yes Every code the dataset emits: code, description, source_table. policy.yaml yes The dataset policy, below. hooks/ no Python for what no reader option can express. See Hooks. converters/ no The dataset's own family converters, listed in dataset.yaml. tasks/ no Task templates and their cohorts.

dataset.yaml:

Field Required Meaning description yes unit (what one subject is), time (the kind of time: date and time, visit dates only, seconds from start) and version (the dataset release). units yes The table and column that list every subject. source yes The source population: salt and the default fraction, or all. verify no What to check before reading, beyond the files the readers list. See Verify. read yes A list of format readers, each with what it reads. See Format readers. rules no Visit and timing rules. See Visit rules. definitions no Named definitions, such as a disease, that recipes use. Core leaves their form to the builder; medomni-v1 reads them as cohort requirements. See Recipes. converters no The dataset's own family converters: files in the package, such as converters/h5_to_edf.py, each defining CONVERTER. Core loads them by path. storage_mb no The disk space each atom task gets, in MB. 16,384 when absent; BDSP sets 65,536.

docs.title: Format readers
docs.text:
Each entry in read names a reader and its options:

read:
- reader: csv
  options:
    tables:
      admissions:
        file: hosp/admissions.csv
        subject: subject_id
        subject_type: int
        time: admittime
        visit: hadm_id
        events:
        - code: ADMISSION
        - {code: DISCHARGE, time: dischtime}
      labevents:
        file: hosp/labevents.csv
        subject: subject_id
        time: charttime
        events:
        - {code: "LAB//{itemid}", value: valuenum}
- reader: tree
  options:
    files:
      cxr-radiograph-2d: {pattern: "cxr/{subject}/{record}.png"}
      psg-night: {pattern: "psg/{subject}/{record}.h5", format: h5, families: [eeg-sleep-6ch-200hz-uv]}

csv reads tables, as CSV or Parquet. Per table:

Field Required Meaning file yes The file, relative to your copy. A glob, such as waves/*.csv, reads every match as one table. subject yes The subject column. subject_type no str (default) or int. time no The time column. time_from no For rows with no time of their own: {table, key, column}, the time of the other table's row with the same key. Not with time. visit no The visit column. events yes The codes each row emits. See the event fields below. where no Keep only rows whose column holds one of the listed values: {column: [values]}. clean no How a column's text is cleaned before codes are filled from it: before (keep the text before this, stripped), remove (drop these characters), lower. load no false: the table is read for evidence but not loaded into the event table, for a table too large to load. Default true. missing_time no drop: a row whose time is empty emits nothing. Default keep.

A table with neither time nor time_from holds static facts.

Each event:

Field Required Meaning code yes The code. {column} is filled from that column, as in LAB//{itemid}. value no A numeric column. text no A text column. time no A time column other than the table's. path for FILE// codes The file or folder, relative to your copy; {column} is filled. present no Emit only when these columns are filled. absent no Emit only when these columns are empty. equals no Emit only when the column holds one of these values: {column: [values]}. 
events:
- {code: DEATH, time: deathtime, present: [deathtime]}
- {code: DEATH, time: dischtime, absent: [deathtime], equals: {hospital_expire_flag: ["1"]}}

tree finds files by folder pattern. Per entry:

Field Required Meaning pattern yes The path, relative to your copy, with {subject} and {record}. format no family (default): the files are in the family the entry is named by. h5: one raw night per file, which a family converter turns into several families. families for h5 The families an h5 file carries. per_subject no Files per subject (default 1). exclude no Skip a path that holds any of these strings. subject_from no {table, key}: the path's {subject} is a value of the table's key column, mapped to that table's subject. A path whose key isn't in the table is skipped.

Hidden files and empty files are skipped.

hook runs a hook: {hook: <name>, params: {...}}.

docs.title: Hooks
docs.text:
A hook is Python for what no reader option can express, at studio/datasets/<dataset>/hooks/<name>.py. A hook reader names it; hooks run after the other readers, in the order listed.

read:
- reader: hook
  options: {hook: ckd, params: {creatinine: [LAB//50912, LAB//52546]}}
Function Required Does derive(rows, raw_root, params) yes Returns new event rows. rows are the rows read so far, which it must not change; it may also read raw files. inputs(raw_root, params) no The raw files it reads, relative to your copy. They are checked before loading, and they join the cache key. dummy(raw_root, subjects, params, rng) no Writes those raw files for a dummy copy. subjects maps each subject id to its start time. problems(raw_root, params) no Problems in your copy, which medomni studio data check reports.

Every code a hook emits is listed in codes.csv with source_table hook:<name>.

Two more hooks are found by their names, and no reader runs them:

  • views, which the evidence rules name: it gives the forms the agent reads. When the package has verify.unit_files, it may also define dummy_unit(path, rng), which writes one unit's file for dummy data.
  • download, at hooks/download.py: it tells medomni studio download-list where the dataset's files come from. index_files() gives the index tables to fetch first, and files(raw_root, params, rows) the files of the source population's patients, chosen from those tables. Each entry is a source, the path in your copy, and how to fetch it: file, folder or gunzip. A package with no download hook is listed by its tree patterns.

The hooks in v0.3.0:

Dataset Hook Does AI-READI views The participant's demographics, and the measurement and observation rows as one table. BDSP download Keys under BDSP's S3 access point: the index tables, then each patient's latest night. BDSP psg Each patient's latest night on disk: its start and end, the families it carries, its sleep metrics and the demographics. rate_enforced lists families a night only carries when the family accepts the night's native rate. It is also the evidence rules' views. MIMIC-IV download PhysioNet: core and ED whole, then the chest films, ECGs and bedside waveforms of the source population. MIMIC-IV ckd CKD by KDIGO from blood creatinine, and the end of each patient's creatinine span. MIMIC-IV cxr One row per frontal chest film (PA, AP), timed by the study's date and time. MIMIC-IV wdb Bedside waveforms and numerics: one row per segment and family, and one per numerics file. MIMIC-IV views Demographics, labs, ED vitals and outpatient measurements as one table, image sizes, and crop_file for the numerics. VitalDB download VitalDB's open API: the clinical, lab and track tables, then each case's .vital file. VitalDB views The case's demographics, the lab rows as one table, and dummy_unit for .vital files. Lab times are dates counted from 2000-01-01 00:00:00, the start of the case, the moment the EDF recordings start; surgical times stay in seconds from the start of the case.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
Before loading, every table file the readers list and every file a hook's inputs names must exist. verify adds:

Check Meaning version The copy's release, which must equal description.version: {file, key} reads a field of a JSON file, or {file, contains, version} gives version when the file contains the text. manifests A glob of tab-separated manifests. Every file their filepath or file_path columns list must exist. unit_files A path pattern with {unit}, such as cases/{unit}.vital. The file must exist for every unit. 
verify:
  manifests: "*/manifest.tsv"
  version: {file: dataset_description.json, key: version}

docs.title: Visit rules
docs.text: Rule Meaning visit: unit The subject is the visit: one case, one visit. one_visit: <code> Each subject has exactly one <code> event, and every event belongs to its visit. untimed: true An event with no time takes the time of the subject's one_visit event, for cross-sectional data. Needs one_visit.

docs.title: Policy file
docs.text: Field Required Meaning dataset yes Dataset id, matching its package folder, such as mimic-iv. version yes The dataset release the policy was read against. access yes open or credentialed. license yes id and url of the license or data use agreement. modules no Per-module overrides where modules carry different licenses. publish yes For each kind of output (schema, templates, recipes, id_lists, labels, per_record_derived, samples): allow, conditional or deny. routes yes local and cloud, each allow, conditional or deny. route_conditions no What a conditional route requires, such as verified zero retention. use yes Whether commercial use is allowed, and any restriction on purpose. attribution no The notice a published sample must carry. sources yes The license, agreement and FAQ pages the policy was read from.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Use only a route the policy allows. Before a run, Bench refuses a route the policy denies, and prints the route_conditions of a conditional route: it runs, and you must meet each condition. A dataset with no policy allows only local.
  • Nothing marked deny under publish is ever uploaded or published. For credentialed datasets, templates, recipes and config hashes ship instead of data.
  • MedOmni's public Hugging Face repository holds dummy data only. No real record is published there, whatever the policy allows.

docs.title: Model card
docs.text:
Contract: model card, src/medomni/core/contracts/schemas/model-card.schema.json. One per encoder, at perception/encoders/<family>/<encoder>/card.yaml, and published to Hugging Face.

Field Required Meaning id yes <family>__<name>, matching the encoder's folder. family yes The one family it reads. modality yes The modality, in plain words. summary yes One sentence on what it does. authors yes Who built the encoder: name and GitHub handle for each. intended_use no The population and acquisition it was built for. limits no Known conditions where it is out of distribution. outputs yes Each output block's kind (labels, events, text, embedding), with its scale, full labels vocabulary or dim where relevant. options no Option name to description. reliability yes status (unmeasured or measured) and optional evidence. non_training yes Whether it runs zero-shot, with no training on MedOmni data. license yes License of the code and weights. source yes url and rev of the upstream code. weights no uri and sha256 of the weights. runtime no image and digest of the container. acceptance yes pending or accepted, set by review.

A model card has no extra keys, its family exists, and an encoder never returns a label outside its declared vocabulary.

docs.title: Families
docs.text:
The fields of a family file and of aliases.yaml. Families explains how the registry is used.

Contract: family registry, one file per family in core/families/<id>.yaml, plus core/families/aliases.yaml.

docs.title: Family file
docs.text: Field Required Meaning id yes Family id; equals the file name. read_by yes What reads it: deep-encoder, rule-extractor or direct. protocol.format yes Accepted file formats: edf, wfdb, dicom, image, omh, table, json-manifest. protocol.channels / protocol.roles for EDF and WFDB The exact montage or a channel count, or a role vocabulary that at least one channel must match. protocol.rate_hz no Sampling rate; null means unchecked. protocol.units no Dominant unit; null means unchecked. protocol.ndim yes Dimensionality of the data. protocol.dtype yes Data type of the values, such as float32, int16 or uint8. protocol.range no Plausible value range, [min, max] in units, such as [50, 100] for SpO2 in %. Null means unchecked. status yes declared (shape known), supplied (measured on real data) or deprecated. samples no Where the family's published sample files live: dummy or test data, never real records. samples_access no controlled when the family's real sample set is access-controlled: PPG, 12-lead ECG, chest X-ray, irregular clinical measurements and sleep EEG. An encoder of such a family is served when it passes its test data.

docs.title: Aliases
docs.text:
aliases.yaml lists, per family:

  • channel and role relabels
  • extra sampling rates
  • label prefixes
  • DICOM colour modes

Reusable alias blocks are declared once under vocab and referenced by name.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• A sample file opens in a declared format, carries every declared channel, matches rate_hz within 2% (or an alias rate), matches units and dtype, and has its values inside range.
  • Sample content is not degenerate: no flat channels, constant images or empty tables.
  • The same rules apply to every file Build stages and every input the encoder check uses: a file outside its family's range stops the build.

docs.title: Check
docs.text:
medomni contracts check families

It checks every family file, its samples and the aliases.

docs.title: Gateway API
docs.text:
Every endpoint, field and error code of the gateway. Gateway explains how it works.

Contract: Gateway API, src/medomni/core/contracts/schemas/gateway-api.schema.json, with the evidence in evidence.schema.json.

The gateway also serves its own OpenAPI page at /docs.

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Endpoints:

Call Route Returns list_encoders GET /encoders with optional q, family, modality, kind, label, runnable, limit Encoder summaries, best match first get_card GET /cards/{encoder_id} The encoder's model card, verbatim encode POST /encode Evidence GET /families Each family with its encoder counts

Encode request:

Field Type Required Meaning encoder_id string yes <family>__<name>. path string yes The input, relative to the gateway's data root. options object no Encoder options, as declared in its model card.

Evidence (the response):

Field Type Required Meaning encoder_id, family string yes Which encoder answered. healthy bool yes false: the input was degenerate. This is a valid result. outputs list yes The encoder's native output blocks: labels, events, text or embedding. notes list of string yes Why the output is degraded, if it is. reliability object or null yes The model card's reliability block. card object yes The model card, verbatim. provenance object yes input_sha256, input_complete, image_id, and when known weights_sha256, source_rev, image, image_digest. fingerprint string yes sha256: plus 64 hex: the hash of encoder, weights, image, input and options. Identical requests give identical fingerprints. runtime object yes container_start_ms, cached, and optionally duration_ms.

Output blocks:

  • labels: a scale (probability, logit, score or physical) and items of label, value and optional unit
  • events: items with t_start and t_end, in seconds from the start of the recording

docs.title: Rules
docs.text:
• Unknown request fields are rejected (422).
  • Unknown encoder: 404. Path outside the data root or missing: 400. Encoder with a model card but no image: 409. Container crash or a reply naming the wrong encoder or family: 502. No free slot: 503.

docs.title: Check
docs.text: The tests in tests/perception/ check the gateway against this contract: test_gateway_api.py covers the routes, the status codes, the rejected fields and the evidence, against a stand-in pool with no Docker. Requests and replies are messages, not files in the repository, so medomni contracts check does not read them.

docs.title: Recipes
docs.text:
The fields of a cohort file, a label library and an evidence file, the shared codes, and two worked examples. The recipe format is the input of MedOmni's builder, medomni-v1. Recipes explains how the parts fit.

Format: recipe, in src/medomni/studio/schemas/: recipe.schema.json (cohort), recipe-tests.schema.json (test patients), recipe-labels.schema.json and recipe-evidence.schema.json.

docs.title: Times and windows
docs.text:
Windows are written relative to the prediction time or an event:

  • anchor: the prediction time
  • anchor.event: the anchor event itself, before the offset
  • anchor + 7 days, anchor - 24 hours: an offset; units minutes, hours, days
  • visit:<code>: the time of that code in the anchor's visit

from and to bound a window. from is included and to is included unless include_from or include_to is false. A missing bound is open.

docs.title: Cohort file
docs.text:
studio/datasets/<dataset>/tasks/<template>/cohorts/<cohort>.yaml

Field Required Meaning version yes The version N.X of the tasks built from this cohort, as a quoted string such as "1.0". Unquoted, YAML reads it as a number and 1.10 becomes 1.1, so the contract refuses it. source yes The source population: all, or {fraction: f} for the hash rule with the dataset's salt. Omitting fraction uses the dataset's default. anchor yes The prediction time: event (a code), pick (first or last; default first), plus (an offset). require no A list of requirements, all of which must hold. select yes How cohort selection picks patients: n (patients in all), by (target names that define the classes; empty for a continuous target), balance (labels from the library that split each class into groups; never scored or shown), seed (a number or text).

A requirement is one of:

Form Holds when any: [codes] at least one of the codes occurs in the window none: [codes] none of the codes occurs in the window files: [families] the patient has a file in each family in the window has_label: <target> the target's label has a value definition: <name> the dataset's named definition holds converts: {min_families: n} at least n of the patient's files convert and match their family; checked during cohort selection, going down the ranking, and a patient who fails is replaced by the next one

any, none and files take from, to and same_visit: true (only events in the anchor's visit count). Codes may be patterns: ^DIAGNOSIS//ICD//(N17|584).

Test patients: cohorts/<cohort>.tests.yaml, a list of patients, each with events (rows of the event table) and expect: in (true or false), and when in, anchor and the label values.

docs.title: Label library
docs.text:
studio/datasets/<dataset>/labels.yaml: one entry per label, named <dataset>:<label> in templates.

Field Meaning exists 1 when a matching code occurs in the window, else 0. none 1 when no matching code occurs in the window, else 0. value The code whose value is read. pick Which value: first, last (default), min, max. op, x Compare the value with x (<, <=, ==, >=, >), giving 1 or 0. bins Cut points; gives the bin index, 0 to the number of cuts. cases, else Ordered when (a rule) and then (the result); the first that holds wins. default The result when no event is found. Without it, the patient has no label. from, to The window, as above. Required; any marks a label read from any time, which Build flags. same_visit, other_visit Count only events in the anchor's visit, or only events in other visits, such as for a readmission. They exclude each other. hook A Python function in the package's hooks/, for a label no rule can express. guard What would reveal the answer: codes (patterns) and fields (table columns). Removed from the evidence. question The sentence that tells the agent exactly what the target asks. A template's target may replace it. Each target needs one, here or in the template.

Each label has exactly one rule: exists, none, value, cases or hook.

Named definitions are in the package's dataset.yaml, under definitions, each a requirement as above.

docs.title: Evidence file
docs.text:
studio/datasets/<dataset>/evidence.yaml: tables, static, files, views and reading_note.

Per table:

Field Meaning time The column compared with the prediction time. A date-only value counts as the end of that day. An empty value is kept. time_from Time the row by a linked row instead: {table, key, column}. missing_time: drop drops rows with no linked time. visit The visit column. skip_index_visit: true drops rows of the anchor's visit. end, blank_after_end When the row's end is after the prediction time, blank these fields. missing_end says whether an empty end counts as after or before. blank_in_index_visit Fields blanked on the anchor's visit, at any time. guard.fields names the guard fields of the template's labels. drop guard: drop rows whose emitted code matches a guard code of the template's labels. keep_if_kept Keep a row only when its key is in another table's kept rows: {table, key}. write_empty Write the table, header only, when the patient has no rows.

static: the patient's static facts. blank names the fields to blank, or guard.fields; aliases maps a static field to the column, or columns, that hold it.

files: files are kept when their time is at or before the prediction time; an untimed file is kept. crop lists families whose files have no time of their own but hold rows from after it, such as one table of a whole stay: each such file is cut at the prediction time by the views hook's crop_file, and staged as a copy.

The rest of the file:

Field Meaning views A hook in the package's hooks/ that gives the forms the agent reads. Its functions are optional: demographics (the patient's static facts), measurements (the kept rows as one long table, read by the clinical-measurement-irregular family), file_meta (details of a file, such as an image's size), crop_file (for files.crop). reading_note A fact about reading this dataset's files, told to the agent in every arm.

docs.title: Template fields that use the recipe
docs.text:
In template.yaml:

Field Meaning targets Each with name, label (a library entry), metric (auc, qwk or mae), and an optional question that replaces the label's. input, exclude What the proposal named to show and to remove. A record only: the evidence is the whole record minus the targets' guards.

The other template fields are in Tasks reference.

docs.title: Shared codes
docs.text:
Every dataset that has these concepts uses these codes. All other codes are the dataset's own, listed in its codes.csv.

Code Meaning ADMISSION, DISCHARGE Start and end of a hospital stay DEATH Death ICU_ADMISSION Start of an ICU stay DIAGNOSIS//ICD//<code> A diagnosis code, ICD-9 or ICD-10, without the dot FILE//<family> A file in a family, with its path RECORDING//START, RECORDING//END Start and end of a recording, such as a sleep study

docs.title: Example: MIMIC-IV, coagulation disorder at 24 hours
docs.text:
template.yaml (part):

targets:
  - {name: coagulation_hemorrhagic, label: mimic-iv:coagulation-hemorrhagic, metric: auc}
input:
  tables: [admissions, labevents, ed_vitalsign]
  families: [cxr-radiograph-2d, ecg-12lead-500hz-mv]

labels.yaml (entry):

coagulation-hemorrhagic:
  exists: ^DIAGNOSIS//ICD//(D65|D66|D67|D68|D69|286|287)
  from: visit:ADMISSION
  to: visit:DISCHARGE
  guard: {codes: ['^DIAGNOSIS//ICD//(D65|D66|D67|D68|D69|286|287)']}
  question: Your prediction is the probability that the patient's record carries a coded diagnosis of a coagulation or hemorrhagic disorder.

cohorts/n20.yaml:

version: "1.0"
source: {fraction: 0.05}
anchor: {event: ADMISSION, pick: first, plus: 24 hours}
require:
  - any: [DISCHARGE, DEATH]           # the stay has ended in the data
    same_visit: true
  - none: [DISCHARGE, DEATH]          # still in hospital at the prediction time
    from: anchor.event
    to: anchor
    same_visit: true
select: {n: 20, by: [coagulation_hemorrhagic], seed: 7}

Built as mimic-iv_coag-hemorrhagic@n20.

docs.title: Example: VitalDB, creatinine after surgery
docs.text:
labels.yaml (entry):

cr_max_7d:
  value: LAB//cr
  pick: max
  from: anchor
  include_from: false
  to: anchor + 7 days
  guard: {codes: [LAB//cr], fields: [preop_cr]}
  question: Your prediction is the numeric value of the highest blood creatinine (mg/dL) in the 7 days after the end of this operation.

cohorts/n20.yaml:

version: "1.0"
source: all
anchor: {event: OP//END}
require:
  - any: [LAB//cr]                    # a creatinine before the end of surgery
    to: anchor
  - has_label: cr_max_7d
select: {n: 20, by: [], seed: 7}          # a numeric target: no classes

The guard removes every creatinine row and the pre-operative creatinine field from the evidence, including values from before the end of surgery. The requirement still uses them to choose patients.

docs.title: Tasks
docs.text:
The task template, the built files, the config hash, and the benchmarks and their task sets. Templates and cohorts are the input of MedOmni's builder, medomni-v1; the built files and task sets are Core contracts that Bench reads. Tasks explains how they fit together.

Format: task template, src/medomni/studio/schemas/task-template.schema.json, read by medomni-v1. The cohort fields are in Recipes.

docs.title: Tasks in v0.3.0
docs.text:
One folder per template in studio/datasets/<dataset>/tasks/, with its cohorts.

  • 30 templates on credentialed data: 15 on AI-READI, 9 on MIMIC-IV, 6 on BDSP
  • 3 templates on VitalDB, on open data
  • an n20 cohort for every template, and a ladder cohort for the 5 templates of the modality ladder, whose rungs are in each template's arms/modality-ladder.yaml

docs.title: Task template
docs.text:
studio/datasets/<dataset>/tasks/<template>/template.yaml

Field Required Meaning template_id yes <dataset>_<name>; equals the folder name. dataset yes The dataset the template binds to. authors yes Who wrote the template: name and GitHub handle for each. targets yes One or more. Each has a name, a label from the dataset's library, and its metric: auc, qwk or mae. An optional question replaces the label's. input yes The tables and families the proposal named. A record only: the evidence is the patient's whole record minus the targets' guards. evidence no The evidence variants: [default] (default). v0.3.0 builds only default and refuses <template>:full@<cohort>. exclude no Codes or fields the proposal asked to remove. A record only, like input. agent yes What an agent needs to run the task: the four fields below. agent.statement yes The clinical question alone. Every atom task's instruction opens with it. agent.instruction yes The template's own paragraph on the prediction time. Build adds the rest of the instruction. agent.environment yes CPUs, memory, internet access, agent and verifier timeouts. agent.submission_path yes Where the agent writes its answer.

Check a template, its cohort and the build; the exit code is 1 on any failure:

medomni studio task check <template>@<cohort>

docs.title: Built files
docs.text:
Build writes each task's content once, then renders it into atom tasks under each arm. The files Bench reads are the built-task contract; record.json is medomni-v1's own.

The content is in atomtasks/_content/<template>@<cohort>/, such as atomtasks/_content/mimic-iv_ckd-staging@n20/:

Path Holds content.json The atom list, the targets and their metrics, each atom's prediction time, the task version, the step counts. answers.csv Each patient's answer for every target. manifest.json The build manifest: the config hash under each arm and variant, the builder (medomni-v1/<version>), the step counts and the release. <atom>/record.json The evidence the instruction shows, as structured data.

An atom task is what an agent runs, rendered under atomtasks/<arm>/<atom>/, or atomtasks/<arm>/<variant>/<atom>/ for an arm with variants, such as atomtasks/modality-ladder/r1/<atom>/. Rendering stages the patient's files from the cache. Its files are real copies, never links:

Path Holds task.toml Task metadata, arm, resources, the <template>@<cohort> and the patient. instruction.md The clinical question, the prediction time, the patient's record, and each target with its question. environment/ The closed-network containers, with the perception service when the arm attaches it. tests/ expected.json (the target names) and format_check.py, a format check on the answer. It never scores. data/ The patient's staged files, minus anything that leaks a target.

The answers stay in the content folder; a render never copies them into an atom task. The atom tasks of one <template>@<cohort> are scored together against them.

docs.title: Config hash
docs.text:
Each <template>@<cohort> under each arm, or arm variant, has a config hash: cfg1: and the SHA-256 over its config files, the builder and two release names. Each file adds its path, its length and its bytes, in path order.

  • The files: the ones the builder's config_files names. For medomni-v1, the template, the cohort, the labels and recipes the task uses, and the arm's definition with its variant.
  • The builder: its name and version, such as medomni-v1.
  • The releases: the dataset release and the MedOmni release.

Build writes it to the build manifest, beside the step counts. Run and score records copy it as config_hash. The prefix names the algorithm, so published config hashes stay checkable after an upgrade. It covers no data.

medomni studio task check --release checks every pinned pair in every task set of the workspace's benchmarks. It fails when a pair's cohort, labels, targets, scoring or dataset release differs from the last release and its N has not risen. It compares config files only. MedOmni runs it before a release; your builds and runs never do.

Result records imported from v0.2 runs are version 0 and carry a v0.2: config hash instead, over the v0.2 template's config files. Only imported records may carry one. They name the sets medomni-bench/v0.2-ladder, v0.2-forced and v0.2-mid, one per v0.2 task tree with runs.

docs.title: Benchmarks and task sets
docs.text:
A benchmark is one folder, bench/benchmarks/<benchmark>/: its card in benchmark.yaml, and its task sets in sets/<set>.yaml. A task set is named <benchmark>/<set>.

Contract: benchmark card, src/medomni/core/contracts/schemas/benchmark.schema.json.

Field Required Meaning name yes The benchmark's name; equals the folder name. version yes The benchmark's own version. owner yes Who maintains it. license yes The license of the benchmark's own files. Each dataset keeps its own license. accepts yes The intelligence kinds it may be run with: agent.

A task set pins each <template>@<cohort> at its version N, and nothing else. Task sets only grow, and an entry never changes: a new N enters only a new task set. The set's content hash, task_set_hash, covers the pairs and their N.

Contract: task set, src/medomni/core/contracts/schemas/task-set.schema.json.

Field Required Meaning name yes The task set's name, such as v1; equals the file name. description no One line on what it holds. builder yes The task builder that builds the set, such as medomni-v1. arms yes The arms every pair is built under. tasks yes One or more entries {task: <template>@<cohort>, version: <N>}, with N an integer. Imported v0.2 sets use 0.

medomni-bench, MedOmni's own benchmark: version 1.0, owner MedOmni team, license CC-BY-4.0, accepts agent.

Task set Data Arms Holds medomni-bench/smoke-dummy Dummy data encoders One pair per template, on generated data. medomni-bench/vitaldb VitalDB encoders, no-perception The 3 VitalDB templates at n20. medomni-bench/v1 AI-READI, MIMIC-IV, BDSP encoders, no-perception The 30 credentialed templates at n20. medomni-bench/modality-ladder AI-READI, MIMIC-IV, BDSP modality-ladder The 5 ladder templates at their ladder cohort.
